The building standards included in the following parts of the 2025 California Building Standards Code, Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations, are adopted by reference and incorporated in this code, except as expressly amended or superseded by the provisions of this code: A. The CBC, including Appendices C, I, and Q, which is based on and which amends the provisions of the 2024 International Building Code ... other_quotes.quote: As of January 1, 2026, the City of Sacramento is requiring all new plan review and permit applications to comply with the 2025 California Building Standards Codes and applicable City Code Amendments.
"CBC" means the California Building Code, 2025 Edition, Volumes 1 and 2. ... "CPC" means the California Plumbing Code, 2025 Edition.

building.note: The city's building code amendments (Chapter 15.20) are three: lit address signs on new buildings (502.1.1), efficiency dwelling units (1208.5) and exits in agricultural buildings (Appendix C). None touches toilet rooms, interior finishes or permits. Unlike San Diego, Sacramento adopts the whole state building code, including its administrative chapter.

permit.exempt_list_quote: When a permit is not required. A permit is not required in some cases. The following is a list of work exempt* from a permit: One-story detached accessory structures, provided the floor area is not greater than 120 square feet. Fences not over 7 feet high. (3) Retaining walls that are not over 4 feet in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge. Water tanks supported directly on grade if the capacity is not greater than 5,000 gallons and the ratio of height to diameter or width does not exceed 2 to 1. Sidewalks and driveways. (1) Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. (2) Prefabricated swimming pools that are less than 18 inches deep. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. Window awnings supported by an exterior wall that do not project more than 54 inches from the exterior wall and do not require additional support. Decks not exceeding 200 square feet in area, that are not more than 30 inches above grade at any point, are not attached to a dwelling and do not serve the exit door required by Section R311.2 of the California Residential Code. * Unless within a design review or historic preservation district (or a historic landmark). (1) Permits and approval from other City departments may be required. (2) Related work may require a building permit, such as relocating electrical fixtures to accommodate new cabinets or counters.

permit.partitions_note: The city's own list does not mention partitions at all. The state code list it points to (section 105.2) exempts 'nonfixed and movable ... partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches', without naming toilet partitions or saying whether floor-anchored or overhead-braced compartments count. The city's exemptions do not apply in a design review or historic preservation district or to a historic landmark. The question is left open here.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Sacramento job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Sacramento government offices, schools, hospitals and warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Sacramento uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Sacramento requires a permit for remodeling and follows California's list of work that needs none. Its exempt list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work", and the state list adds movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. Neither names toilet partitions, so ask the Building Division's public counter (916-808-5318) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Sacramento Building Division
page.stalls_intro: Sacramento counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of Sacramento Building Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: In Sacramento, contractors pay the city's business operations tax when a building permit is issued, and permits go to the owner, the owner's agent or a licensed contractor. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Sacramento the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Sacramento County that is $68.58 an hour plus $34.95 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.75% in Sacramento: 7.25% statewide, 0.5% for the county transportation authority and 1% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Government offices and public buildings:** stainless steel or phenolic that stands up to heavy daily use.
